Role Overview

The Product Knowledge Specialist creates, maintains, and improves product knowledge so customers and internal teams can easily find and trust the information they need. You'll use MadCap Flare, approved AI-enabled tools, and other knowledge platforms to develop clear, accurate, reusable, and accessible content.

You will report to Director Product Management.

Main Responsibilities

  • Create, update, organize, and publish product documentation, user guidance, release communications, and other knowledge content.
  • Use MadCap Flare and approved tools to develop structured, reusable, and easy-to-find content.
  • Partner with Product Managers, Engineering, and subject matter experts to turn complex product information into clear and accessible knowledge.
  • Follow established standards for content quality, metadata, versioning, publishing, and lifecycle management.
  • Identify outdated, missing, duplicated, or unclear information and collaborate with the appropriate teams to resolve gaps.
  • Support content migration, consolidation, and continuous improvement of the knowledge environment.
  • Use approved AI-enabled tools to support drafting, summarization, classification, metadata, and quality review while applying human judgment to ensure accuracy.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, or automate knowledge processes and continue developing expertise in product knowledge practices.

Experience and Skills

  • 1+ years of experience creating or managing technical, product, customer, or knowledge content, or comparable experience working with structured information.
  • Collaborate effectively with subject matter experts and cross-functional teams.Learning new technologies, tools, and ways of working.
  • Use approved AI-enabled tools responsibly, applying appropriate human judgment and quality controls.

What You'll Bring

  • Familiarity with U.S. healthcare, revenue cycle, or healthcare technology.
  • Experience with MadCap Flare or similar structured authoring and publishing tools.
  • Familiarity with structured authoring, content reuse, metadata, taxonomy, or knowledge management.
  • Experience with source control, multi-author workflows, search optimization, knowledge repositories, or content migration.
